goal: Every card the Home surface mounts is described by content (`blocks[]`, `actions[]`, `empty`, `delivery`) and drawn by the block renderer through a skin — no per-card web view on `/app`. When this programme is done the ledger's home keys are gone, the hero's home mode is torn down, and Home is the first *surface* — not card — that MSR renders end to end, which is the precondition for the performance programme that follows (a surface that is one derivation + one renderer can be measured, seeded and bundled as one unit).

contract: The product's appearance survives the migration: the existing stylesheets are the asset, dressed back on through skins; new CSS only where no old rule exists to reuse. The rulings the steps name (R-H3, R-H4, R-H5, R-H6) are Martin's: a step that reaches one unmade goes blocked with blocked_by naming it, and does not improvise.
No new vocabulary (block kind, mark, tone) without a ruling — an addition is a stop, never an edit.

The reader and compose covers (email-window-layout), and everything inbox (inbox-finish).
The planning surface beyond the trio of cards Home itself mounts — the rest is planning-on-msr.
The performance programme the goal names as following this project — measured after, not built here.

steps.title: H0a · The port data, and the keys that can be taken today
steps.done_when: sdk/corpus/ports/ holds a recording per home mount and sdk/corpus/legacy/ an answer key at every class for the six cards mountable alone; legacy-comparison.test.js green. (Delivered — see What the code taught us.)
instruction: **H0 · Freeze the answer key** *(no product change).* Split in two by what the code turned out to allow — see *What the code taught us*.
comments: **2026-08-30, H0a.** Four things, each of which changed how H0 is built rather than what it is for.
**A capture's port data lives in a scenario, and a scenario for an unmigrated card is red**

**A capture's port data lives in a scenario, and a scenario for an unmigrated card is red.** `msr-legacy-projection-capture.mjs` reads `sdk/corpus/cards/<key>.json`; `sdk/tooling/card-corpus.mjs` runs every file in that directory and fails one whose card has no registered derivation, with a reason. That is the corpus gate working, and it is incompatible with H0's order — capture every key BEFORE the first derivation, so no derivation's shape can leak into the key it will be measured against. So the port data got its own artifact, `sdk/corpus/ports/`, recorded by `scripts/msr-card-port-record.mjs` through the product's own query bindings, and it MOVES into the scenario at the card's migration rather than being copied. Two gates hold that: a card with both is refused, and a recording nothing captures is refused.
**A capture with no comparison is red too**

**A capture with no comparison is red too**, for the same structural reason: a comparison mounts the migrated card and needs its derivation. Between H0 and each card's own post there is an answer key with no reader, and that state is now declared (`AWAITING_MIGRATION`, one entry per card naming the post that closes it) rather than tolerated. An entry whose card HAS a comparison is red, so the declaration cannot hide a reader from the gate.
**The four hero children have no view of their own**

**The four hero children have no view of their own.** `card-views.js` registers `home-hero-postcard`, `-weather`, `-priority-rail` and `-fun-rail` as `parentOwnedChildView`, whose `render` returns null: the hero draws all four inside its own element in home mode. This is stronger evidence for R-H3 than the plan's own reading — the parent does not merely draw nothing of its own, the children draw nothing of theirs — and it means their answer keys need the capture to mount the parent and project a named slot. Their port data is recorded; the capture is H0b's first piece.

**The device classes are 599 / 899 / 900, not 599 / 899 / 1280.** The capture derives each width from the class's own bound in `MSR_DEVICE_CLASS_BOUNDS` and refuses any width that resolves to another class, deliberately — the widths are a value in the contract rather than a behaviour of an instrument. 1280 is not one of them, and the plan's H0 text said it was. Desktop is where `action-home` splits into two columns and drops from eight rows to six, so the class matters and the number is the contract's to give. Two smaller findings, both on the record in the instruments rather than here: `items` has two query bindings declaring the same port with the same query and the same parameters (`msr:query-binding:home:content:items:data-source` and `msr:query-binding:items:home-content:data-source`), which the recorder dedupes and names; and a card can name its rows more than one way — the action/reminder stack keys two lists on `data-action-id` and `data-reminder-id` — so `rowAttribute` now takes a list.

instruction: **H0b · The rest of the keys** *(one PR).* Three pieces, in this order:

The capture learns to mount a PARENT and project a named sub-tree. The four hero children register `parentOwnedChildView`, whose `render` returns null — the postcard and both rails are drawn inside the hero's element by its home-mode hydrate — so they cannot be mounted on their own. Their port data is already recorded and declared `AWAITING_CAPTURE`.

The `items` adapter draws in the harness. Today `hydrate` returns with the card still `card--loading` and `display: none`, no error and no rejection; the keys it produced said the card draws nothing and were deleted rather than committed.

The variant matrix on top of the base keys: hero × daypart (morning/day/evening/night) × theme (light/dark) × rails (filled/empty); today-focus without upcoming events; action-home (empty/filtered); the action/reminder stack with a populated day — the seeded week has nothing due on 2026-08-30, so H0a's key for it is the empty state and H8 needs both; items trip (active/none) and items content (grid, show-more). Per-variant `capturedAt` and a theme are instrument work the capture does not have yet.
Done when `sdk/corpus/ports/` is empty of `AWAITING_CAPTURE` entries, every home card has an answer key at every class, and `MAX_OPEN_BUG_ROWS` is pinned.

instruction: **H5 · `action-home`** — one `list`; rows = actions with `tags` (status, source), `meta` (due), `badge`, `actions` (complete, dismiss, archive-email, open-source, start-session, set-due, set-reminder). **command presentations** (a command whose executor opens a host popover, like `layout.route.open` opens a route) — no new block. Ruling: R-H5. The section's filter chips already live outside the card (section controls).

instruction: **H7 · `items` on Home** — the seed card's two home configs become the first `items` derivation: `entities:trip` → one `detail`-shaped row (the rich trip tile: title, dates, place, travel line, `open`), `content` → a `list` whose rows are the content tiles (`media` thumbnail, title, `meta` updatedAt, `tags` type) with `group.more` for "show more". The skin carries the grid and the mobile horizontal rail; drag-to-scroll stays host choreography. This is also the first cut into the 2 002-line adapter — Home exercises ≈600 lines of it, and those become the derivation; the library-hub two-thirds stay for the library programme. Ruling: R-H7.

steps.title: H8 · The planning trio
steps.done_when: The planning trio reads only content on the view-model tier; the ledger has no home key; the migrated count moves by the measured amount; /app is drawn by the block renderer from one composition.
instruction: **H8 · The planning trio** — view-model tier: each keeps a view that reads only `content` (plan §3, "step 8 is a rewrite against content"). Rhythm and the stack carry an inline `form` (title/start/end; title) — the form host from card 4 (`commit: 'submit'`, segments) is ready. Delete's `window.confirm` becomes `requiresConfirmation` (card 6's host). Week-terrain's segmented load bar has no block field — it is `meta` + a skin verb at most, or a `progress` per segment; measured at H0, decided then. Last, because week-focus's own plan (skeleton layer, mount order) is `ready` and lands first.
After H8: the ledger has no home key; the gate reads `migrated 19 of 108` (6 today + 12 home + label-manager flip), and `/app` is drawn by the block renderer from one composition.

goal: Give MSR a time contract of its own — one lifetime primitive that owns phase, currency, disposal and parent/child order — so the four axes currently carrying time for it (composition, data, rendering, presentation) can each change without touching the others. This is P1 of the axis programme (docs/plans/msr-core-programme.md §4), and its full plan is already written, measured and ruled: docs/plans/msr-p1-time-axis-plan.md (#10806). This PLAN.json is that plan's runnable form — each step is one of its posts, and the prose plan is the instruction of record; what is here is the map, not a copy.

Re-verified at the 2026-09-02 plan review against main (2d735aa574): nothing of P1 is built (no runtime/lifetime.js, no unit-state.js); createCardRuntime still has exactly one production caller behind the flag route; card-node still carries its own mounted/suspended/destroyed machine (card-node.js:95-98) read by planner.js:58,66; the three query consumers still hold their own visibilitychange listeners; bindShellLifecycle still has zero callers; the registry still rejects colons in reasons (surface-runtime-node-registry.js:52). Drift since the plan was written: 33 files with generation counters (was 36), 15 files with isRuntimeDestroyed (was 19 copies). The shape holds; re-run the §2 greps at each step per the plan's own instruction.
contract: The five rulings in the prose plan's §1 are inputs and are not reopened — above all: the justification is structural, and native readiness may not be cited.
The state model moves onto the live path BEFORE the Canvas flag is deleted (ruling 3; tests/architecture/w1-native-readiness-interlock.test.js guards the order).
Post 2b's proof is a browser run of the three surfaces F5.3 broke (home, people, inbox), not a test count.
The LiveCall suspend question before post 5 ships is Martin's ruling, not the plan's default, if device testing shows a call surface degrading.
out_of_scope: Everything the prose plan's §7 lists — P2/P3's deletions, SDK vocabulary, the unsurveyed axes, the 56 hygiene flags, W1's own deletions.
Post 8 — adoption across the ~33 counter files and 15 helper copies — is its own ratcheted project once the primitive exists; open-ended by design.
